text: Spectral elements and FR: small comparisons with existing FEM/DG Compare2D SEM Poisson and1D periodic FR advection with the existing P1 FEM/modal DG under matched equations, boundaries and analytic fields. Separate h/p refinement, continuous error, residuals, conservation and time error from any external Nek/PyFR execution. These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems. Routine supplement CI runs the supplement groups listed in the public registry with NumPy,SciPy and pytest. It checks versions,inputs and execution records for stored independent references and distinguishes their reuse from new reference computations. The existing common22-case suite,including quantum convergence,remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts,criteria and history are preserved. Download and execute the supplement Run inside atlas-sem-fr-2026-11-23 from the ZIP. This command executes all 2 fixed cases in the supplement. The bundled results/ contains stored outputs. Rerun into a new output/ directory, and choose another fresh directory for subsequent runs. python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python -m pytest -q python run.py --input inputs.json --output output Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it. 2D spectral-element Poisson: P1 FEM comparison and h/p refinement Solve a sine manufactured solution on the unit square with GLL spectral elements and the existing triangle P1 FEM. Compare matched free-unknown counts under h refinement and p=1..6 at fixed elements. Methods, equations, figures and references Input and validation protocol history · Initial input Assumptions, units and boundaries Dimensionless: -Laplacian u=2pi²sin(pi x)sin(pi y) on[0,1]², u=0 on the boundary. Constant coefficient; affine Cartesian squares for SEM and the existing regular triangle mesh for P1 FEM. Adopted numerical method C0 tensor Qp Lagrange SEM with p+1 Legendre GLL nodes/quadrature, sparse stiffness assembly and a SciPy direct solve. At p=2 use2/4/8 elements per axis; separately fix2x2 elements and p=1..6. Check h/p refinement, matched-unknown errors, boundary data and true residuals; save actual2D SEM fields and P1 vertices/triangles/values in NPZ. Verification limits and failures One smooth fixed problem only. Meshes, quadrature and algebraic solvers differ: no speed, complexity or universal-accuracy ranking. The diagonal GLL quadrature mass is not the exactly integrated mass of every product. No curved mesh, singular solution, incompressible flow or Nek5000/nekRS run. No external solver installation, execution or performance comparison. 1D periodic FR advection: Radau correction and published DG comparison Transport0.4+sin(2pi x) toT=.25. Execute Gauss-node/Radau FR and the existing modal DG for p=1/2 and8/16/32 cells; measure analytic error, mass and time-integration error. Methods, equations, figures and references Input and validation protocol history · Initial input Assumptions, units and boundaries Dimensionless u_t+u_x=0 on[0,1), periodic boundary, initial0.4+sin(2pi x), analytic0.4+sin(2pi(x-t)). Constant positive speed1 and uniform affine intervals. Adopted numerical method p+1 Gauss solution points, upwind interface flux, Legendre Radau corrections and SSPRK(3,3). Match initial L2 projection, upwind flux and timestep policy to the unchanged published modal DG. Check weighted mass at every RK stage and quadratic energy at each completed step. A matrix exponential of the same FR operator separately measures RK3 time error and its timestep-halving response. Verification limits and failures DG correspondence is for these Radau/Gauss choices, a constant linear flux and affine elements. No all-FR/all-DG equivalence, nonlinear flux, shock, limiter or multidimensional FR claim. Distinguish coupled h/dt refinement from the exponential spatial result; the exponential is not an independent spatial PDE solver. PyFR itself is not run.
